## Configuration and switch evidence {#sec-ch15-ch12-tests}

<!-- PROVENANCE

sources: tests named in the Code table; tests/CMakeLists.txt at the pin

### Summary

A numerical test can pass while exercising the wrong option, loading the wrong package, or accepting a misspelt
key as if it were absent. The configuration tests of @sec-ch12 guard against that: they check a default and its
override through the YAML reader rather than through a direct call, they require an unknown key to be refused
with a message that names it, and they check that a setup guard refuses what the scheme cannot deliver. This
section collects those tests; they are the preconditions for reading the switch matrix of @sec-ch12-matrix.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Ties the chapter 12 claims (package origin, option parsing, key refusal, setup guards) to six registered tests.

**Data.** Parsed booleans, exception messages and the refusal of a split column; no physical quantity.

**Placement.** Verification outside the simulation step, in a build at the code pin.

**Activation.** Select the tests by their ctest name; the seam arms set their switch in the registration.

**Guarantee / limits.** A refusal contract says nothing about the accuracy of the scheme it guards.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch15-ch12-tests-assertions.
:::

Local symbols: none; the YAML boolean `wb-wall-clamp` and the integer
scheme selectors are dimensionless configuration values.

The six tests fall into three groups: the import-path precondition shared with @sec-ch15-ch01, three parser
contracts (an unsupported implicit scheme, the wall-clamp default and override, an unknown geometry key), and
two setup guards of the $x_1$ column split.

### Derivation

Why the catalogue reads these tests the way it does, each step tied to the source at the pin.

1. *Check a default through the parser.* `hydro_options.wb_wall_clamp_ships_enabled`
   ({{< code tests/test_hydro_options.cpp hydro_options.wb_wall_clamp_ships_enabled >}}) writes a minimal card
   with an ideal-gas EOS and no override and requires `wb_wall_clamp()` to be true after `from_yaml`; a direct
   call to the solver would not show what a user's file gets.
2. *Check the override through the same path.* The same case rewrites the card with `wb-wall-clamp: false` and requires the
   parsed value to be false, proving the key is read, not just accepted.
3. *Require a refusal that names the key.* `yaml_keys.geometry_cells_refuses_an_unknown_key`
   ({{< code tests/test_yaml_keys.cpp yaml_keys.geometry_cells_refuses_an_unknown_key >}}) passes `nx4` to
   `expect_refused` ({{< code tests/test_yaml_keys.cpp expect_refused overload=1 >}}), which requires the key
   path to appear in the exception message. Accepting an unused key could silently run the wrong grid.
4. *Require a refusal with a reason.* `hydro_options.reject_unsupported_implicit_scheme`
   ({{< code tests/test_hydro_options.cpp hydro_options.reject_unsupported_implicit_scheme >}}) requires the
   message to contain "Unsupported implicit scheme". `X1SeamSplit.x1_mass_covariance_needs_3_x1_cells`
   ({{< code tests/test_x1_seam_split.cpp X1SeamSplit.x1_mass_covariance_needs_3_x1_cells >}}) requires a
   two-cell block to be refused with "needs at least 3 x1 cells" and a three-cell block to construct without
   throwing. `X1SeamSplit.vic_refuses_x1_split`
   ({{< code tests/test_x1_seam_split.cpp X1SeamSplit.vic_refuses_x1_split >}}) requires one block to step and a
   column split in $x_1$ to be refused with "requires nb1 = 1".
5. *Read none of these as accuracy.* Every row is a boolean, a string or an exception; no row measures the
   error of the scheme it selects, which is the business of the other sections and of @sec-ch15.

### Numerical method

Read the assertion and its registration, then run the selection in a build configured from the code pin
(@fig-ch15-evidence, @sec-ch15). The two seam rows are `seam_arm` registrations that filter the executable to
one case and require exactly one passing test, so an empty filter fails the entry
({{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}). Record device, precision, process count and every skip separately.

: Assertions this catalogue reads. {#tbl-ch15-ch12-tests-sources}

**How to select the tests.** From the repository root, with `build` the directory configured from the code pin,
list the selection and then run it:

```bash
ctest --test-dir build -N -R '^test_(hydro_options|yaml_keys)\.release$'
ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure -R '^test_(hydro_options|yaml_keys)\.release$'
```

The other rows are selected the same way:

```bash
ctest --test-dir build -N -R '^test_python_import_path_python$'
ctest --test-dir build -N -R '^test_x1_seam_split_x1_mass_covariance\.release$'
ctest --test-dir build -N -R '^test_x1_seam_split_vic_refuses_split\.release$'
```

Run each listed selection with `--output-on-failure` in place of `-N`. The clamp case writes its own
minimal card, a parser input rather than a simulation deck:

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `dynamics`[^rg-1c007ea215c1], `equation-of-state`[^rg-5a10d3c13a00], `type`[^rg-c82d9b68904e].
```yaml
dynamics:
  equation-of-state:
    type: ideal-gas
  wb-wall-clamp: false
```

The unknown-key case loads the fixture `test_cycle_diagnostics.yaml` from the build's test directory
({{< code tests/test_yaml_keys.cpp expect_refused overload=2 >}}), so run from the configured build. An empty
selection prints "No tests were found!!!" and is not a result (@sec-ch15).

The contract of the clamp case, from `hydro_options.wb_wall_clamp_ships_enabled`
({{< code tests/test_hydro_options.cpp hydro_options.wb_wall_clamp_ships_enabled >}}):

```cpp
EXPECT_TRUE(snap::HydroOptionsImpl::from_yaml(f)->wb_wall_clamp());
write(f, "  wb-wall-clamp: false\n");
EXPECT_FALSE(snap::HydroOptionsImpl::from_yaml(f)->wb_wall_clamp());
```

`write` truncates and rewrites the card with the override; the two reads of the same file give the default and the override.
No equation is implemented here: this is a precondition for selecting the scheme whose errors @sec-ch15 defines.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_python_import_path_python` | the package origin and the search-path order are right | exact paths; exit 125 when unconfigured | the script |
| `test_hydro_options.release` | an unsupported implicit scheme is refused with a reason | message contains "Unsupported implicit scheme" | the test |
| `test_hydro_options.release` | the wall clamp is on by default and the override is read | boolean equality | the test |
| `test_yaml_keys.release` | an unknown geometry key is refused and named | message contains the key path | `expect_refused` |
| `test_x1_seam_split_x1_mass_covariance.release` | two owned cells are refused with a reason; three are accepted | message contains "needs at least 3 x1 cells"; no throw | the test |
| `test_x1_seam_split_vic_refuses_split.release` | one block steps; a column split in $x_1$ is refused | message contains "requires nb1 = 1" | the test |

: Acceptance criteria at the code pin; CPU run evidence is recorded below, with CUDA coverage limited explicitly. {#tbl-ch15-ch12-tests-assertions}

`expect_refused` has two overloads, one for a card already loaded and one that loads the fixture
({{< code tests/test_yaml_keys.cpp expect_refused overload=1 >}}; {{< code tests/test_yaml_keys.cpp expect_refused overload=2 >}}).
The report-only `src/snapy_report/ch12/checks/configuration_check.py` checks parser truth tables and the reference,
covariance and energy identities on ports; it does not execute the C++ option caches.

The option row checks the default and the explicit override through YAML parsing. The unknown-key
row requires a diagnostic naming the bad key; neither measures the numerical accuracy of a selected
scheme.[^ch15-ch12-run]

### Limits

A minimum-cell guard establishes a refusal contract, not the accuracy of the mass covariance. A runtime result
needs the complete switch environment as well as the package origin, device and rank count; the unmeasured
combinations of @sec-ch12-matrix stay unmeasured here.
